text:
Leo (PM): Dropping a design question: for the private setup wizard network checks, should we present hosts as compact rows (dense table) or as stacked diagnostic cards? Tradeoffs: density vs discoverability. Figma: https://figma.com/file/placeholder

Jon C: I'd vote compact rows for customer lists with >5 hosts. Cards are nice for 1-3 hosts during troubleshooting, but get noisy for fleets.

Maya R: +1 for rows but with an expand-to-card detail. Default show hostname, status pill, and duration (e.g., '2.1s'). On expand, show the diagnostic block and example commands.

Anika (A11y): Important: if we use rows they must be keyboard-focusable and announce status changes. Use aria-live for the global summary and aria-describedby linking each row to its detail region when expanded. Also ensure indicators are non-color dependent (icon + text).

Leo (PM): Good call. For status verbs, keeping them short: 'Reachable', "Can't reach host", 'Timeout', 'Port closed'. Any objections?

Jon C: Minor: 'Timeout' could be ambiguous. Maybe 'No response (timeout)' for clarity in-row and shorter in detail view.

Maya R: UX idea: show a tiny inline 'why' chevron that reveals quick cause and a single action button (Retry probe / Run local check). This avoids sending users to a separate modal.

Anika (A11y): Focus movement rule: when user expands a row, move focus into the first interactive element inside the detail (e.g., Retry) and trap focus inside the expanded area until they hit ESC. That helps keyboard-only users.

Jon C: Technical: we currently run probes in parallel, but response ordering is unpredictable. We should show a subtle 'last updated' timestamp per row so users know which result is freshest.

Leo (PM): About retries: should retry be per-host only, or allow a 'Retry all failed' CTA? I worry about accidental mass retries if customers have rate-limited devices. Thoughts?

Maya R: Offer both but default hide 'Retry all' behind a dropdown or confirmation. For each retry, show an exponential cooldown indicator (e.g., disabled for 30s after 3 attempts) and a tooltip explaining rate limits.

Anika (A11y): Tooltip content must be accessible (aria-describedby) and keyboard reachable. Also ensure the cooldown is announced: 'Retry disabled, try again in 30 seconds' in the live region.

Jon C: Copy suggestion for KB links: replace 'run from a machine in the same network' with 'run from a host on the same VPC or VLAN' — more precise for on-prem customers.

Leo (PM): Noted. Also debating the summary banner tone. Current default is red for any failure; that reads scary. Proposal: use neutral 'Some checks need attention' with an amber icon, and highlight failed counts inside. Anyone hate that?

Maya R: Like it. If all checks pass, banner should be green 'All checks passed' and include a small 'Next' CTA. If mixed, neutral/amber and primary CTA remains 'Fix and retry'.

Anika (A11y): For live updates, avoid too many announcements. Announce only when scan ends and when a user-triggered action finishes. Intermediate changes can update visually without verbose announcements.

ops-bot: probe-run 2026-03-23T15:22:05Z finished (4/6 reachable)

Jon C: ops-bot confirms result — can we include bot output into the detail view (raw logs collapsed by default)? Very helpful for SREs.

Leo (PM): Yes, collapse raw logs behind 'Show raw output' link and make it copyable. For commands, include a one-line copy button next to snippets (e.g., `nc -vz <HOST> <PORT>`).

Maya R: One more microcopy point: use verbs consistently on buttons: 'Retry probe', 'Show details', 'Copy command', 'Retry all failed'. Avoid mixing 'Run' and 'Retry' for probes.

Leo (PM): Great feedback — I'll update the mocks: dense host rows with expand-to-card details, per-row last-updated, per-host retry with cooldown, collapsible raw logs, neutral summary banner copy, and accessible focus/aria behavior. Will post updated figma + preview link when ready.
